text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - German Bunds traded lower nearly all day on Monday, but struggled off early lows in afternoon trading, reinforcing hopes the market can climb later this week. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.20, up 0.06 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts edged higher on Monday in thin trade with investors reluctant to take positions ahead of the budget on Tuesday, dealers said. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 111-05/32, up 08/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bonds climbed slightly on Monday amid renewed optimism about the commitment of European countries to starting a single European currency in 1999 which helped the franc to erase last week's losses against the mark. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.82 up 0.08 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds, Btp futures and the lira recovered after slipping on reports a Rome magistrate was seeking trial for Prime Minister Romano Prodi over abuse of office when he was head of state IRI holding in 1993. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.13 up 0.21 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were higher with the long-end leading the rally in light midday trade as players bought mildly after the release of some friendly existing home sales data, analysts said. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-16/32 up 06/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.42 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures ended down but off their lows on Monday. Selling was sparked by a news report in late afternoon saying Japan's Post Office Life Insurance Bureau had started to become cautious of buying JGBs, traders said. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.75, down 0.05 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market had a quiet session on Monday following heavy issuance last week. Retail-targeted bonds dominated, with a handful of mark deals surfacing. Rheinhyp launched a 500 million mark 10-year bond at a 31 b.p. spread over Bunds. Hokkaido Electric Power set a 300 million mark five-year transaction at 20 b.p. over Bunds. Russia's Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said it would pay Tsarist debts but details were still unclear.
